payload.correction: Holm-Bonferroni, step-down, over all 6 pairwise comparison(s) in this sweep, holding the family-wise error rate at 0.05. Uncorrected, every one of those 6 tests would keep 0.05 of its own; corrected, the tightest threshold any of them has to clear is 0.0083333. Letting a family this size keep 0.05 apiece is the same defect as reporting forty unresolvable deltas and letting somebody believe the tenth.

It is local, it costs no tokens, it sends nothing anywhere, and it is the only one of the four this harness can vary and re-measure for you. WE CANNOT PULL, and these are refusals of honesty rather than of effort: HYBRID BM25 + DENSE RETRIEVAL - a dense retriever needs an embedding model, and this harness ships no AI. rank_bm25, sentence-transformers and faiss are not installed and adding one is a new dependency; the connected Ollama on this machine holds chat models and no embedding model. Who can: you, by connecting an embedding model - at which point every number it produced would be a number about that endpoint, would have to say so, and would mean sending your corpus through it. That is a different tool with a different provenance and a different egress conversation, and it is not this one. A CROSS-ENCODER RERANKER - the same reason with a heavier model attached: a cross-encoder is a model, this harness ships none, and there is no reranker on this machine to call. Who can: you, with your own reranker. The bench would then measure it the same way it measures chunking here - one lever at a time, paired, on the same eval set - because two levers at once is not an experiment. QUERY REWRITING - rewriting a query means asking a model to write a new one, so the recall it produced would be a fact about your connected model and not about your retriever, and this file makes no network call at all. Who can: you, with your own connected model - and the resulting number belongs to that model as much as to the index, which is why it cannot be reported next to these as though it were the same measurement.
